subject: math
title: Grade 5 Area and Perimeter
seo_title: Grade 5 Area and Perimeter Worksheets: Free Math with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Area measurement of squares and rectangles
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 math worksheets on area and perimeter for the BC curriculum: count squares, use area = length × width in cm² and m², find perimeters, work out missing sides, compare rectangles with the same area, and solve garden and field word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Area = length × width (cm², m²). Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width (cm, m).
key_sub: Area is the space inside; perimeter is the distance around. Missing side = area ÷ known side. The same area can have different perimeters.
body_html:
Area: count the squares

Area is the number of unit squares that cover a shape. In a rectangle, the squares sit in equal rows, so you can multiply instead of counting one by one.

Area = length × width

The length tells how many squares fit in each row. The width tells how many rows there are. So area = length × width. Area is in square units: cm² for small things, m² for big spaces like a floor, a garden or a field.

Example

A rectangle is 24 m long and 6 m wide. What is its area?

24 × 6: 20 × 6 = 120 and 4 × 6 = 24. 120 + 24 = 144.

Answer: 144 m²

Perimeter: the distance around

Perimeter is the length of the edge. For a rectangle, add two lengths and two widths: perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width. Perimeter is a length, so it is in cm or m.

Example

A rectangle is 15 cm long and 8 cm wide. What is its perimeter?

2 × 15 + 2 × 8 = 30 + 16 = 46.

Answer: 46 cm

Find a missing side

Know the area? Divide: missing side = area ÷ known side. Know the perimeter? Take away the two sides you know, then halve what is left.

Example

A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 cm. Its length is 9 cm. What is its width?

30 − 9 − 9 = 12 cm for the two widths. 12 ÷ 2 = 6.

Answer: 6 cm

Same area, different perimeter

Two rectangles can have the same area but different perimeters. A long, thin rectangle has a longer perimeter than one that is closer to a square.

Carpet, paint and tiles need the area. A fence, a border or ribbon needs the perimeter.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the sides for the area (8 + 5 = 13)Multiply: 8 × 5 = 40 cm²
Finding the area when the question asks for the perimeterPerimeter goes around: 8 + 5 + 8 + 5 = 26 cm
Writing cm for an area, or cm² for a perimeterArea: cm² or m². Perimeter: cm or m
Adding only one length and one width for the perimeterGo all the way around: 2 lengths + 2 widths
Subtracting to find a missing side (48 − 8 = 40)Divide: 48 ÷ 8 = 6
Mixing units (2 m and 60 cm)Change to one unit first: 2 m = 200 cm

faq.q: What do Grade 5 students learn about area in the BC math curriculum?
faq.a: In Geometry and measurement, Grade 5 students measure the area of squares and rectangles in cm² and m², use area = length × width, and explore how area and perimeter are related.

faq.q: How do you find the area and perimeter of a rectangle?
faq.a: Area = length × width, in square units. Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width, in length units. A rectangle 8 cm by 5 cm has an area of 40 cm² and a perimeter of 26 cm.

faq.q: Can two rectangles have the same area but different perimeters?
faq.a: Yes. A 6 cm by 2 cm rectangle and a 4 cm by 3 cm rectangle both have an area of 12 cm², but their perimeters are 16 cm and 14 cm.

faq.q: What is the difference between cm and cm²?
faq.a: cm measures a length, such as a side or a perimeter. cm² measures an area: the number of 1 cm by 1 cm squares that cover a shape.

sets.title: Find the area by counting squares

items.q: Each small square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: There are 5 rows with 8 squares in each row: 5 × 8 = 40. The area is 40 cm². (26 is the perimeter, the distance around the edge.)

items.q: What is the area of the shaded rectangle in square units?
items.e: There are 4 rows with 7 squares in each row: 4 × 7 = 28. The area is 28 square units. (22 is the perimeter, the distance around the edge.)

items.q: A rectangle is covered by 6 rows of 1 cm² squares, with 9 squares in each row. What is its area?
items.e: 6 rows of 9 squares: 6 × 9 = 54 squares, so the area is 54 cm².

items.q: Each small square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: There are 3 rows with 10 squares in each row: 3 × 10 = 30. The area is 30 cm². (26 is the perimeter, the distance around the edge.)

items.q: Each small square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: There are 3 rows with 8 squares in each row: 3 × 8 = 24. The area is 24 cm². (22 is the perimeter, the distance around the edge.)

items.q: Each small square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded shape?
items.e: Split the shape into two rectangles: 5 × 4 = 20 and 2 × 2 = 4. 20 + 4 = 24 cm². (30 cm² would count the empty corner too.)

items.q: Each small square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded shape?
items.e: Split the shape into two rectangles: 5 × 5 = 25 and 3 × 3 = 9. 25 + 9 = 34 cm². (40 cm² would count the empty corner too.)

items.q: Which multiplication gives the number of squares in this rectangle?
items.e: There are 5 rows of 9 squares. 5 × 9 = 45 squares.

items.q: Only the top row and the left column of squares are drawn. How many squares would cover the whole rectangle?
items.e: The top row shows 7 squares in each row. The left column shows 5 rows. 5 × 7 = 35 squares.

items.q: Why can you multiply to find the number of squares in a rectangle?
c: Every row has the same number
The rows get longer and longer
items.e: In a rectangle, the squares sit in equal rows. Equal groups can be multiplied: number of rows × squares in each row.

items.q: Which multiplication gives the number of squares in this rectangle?
items.e: There are 3 rows of 7 squares. 3 × 7 = 21 squares.

items.q: Only the top row and the left column of squares are drawn. How many squares would cover the whole rectangle?
items.e: The top row shows 9 squares in each row. The left column shows 4 rows. 4 × 9 = 36 squares.

items.q: Each small square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded shape?

items.q: Each small square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded square?
items.e: There are 6 rows with 6 squares in each row: 6 × 6 = 36. The area is 36 cm². (24 is the perimeter, the distance around the edge.)

items.q: Only the top row and the left column of squares are drawn. How many squares would cover the whole rectangle?
items.e: The top row shows 10 squares in each row. The left column shows 4 rows. 4 × 10 = 40 squares.

items.q: What is the area of the shaded rectangle in square units?
items.e: There are 4 rows with 9 squares in each row: 4 × 9 = 36. The area is 36 square units. (26 is the perimeter, the distance around the edge.)

items.q: Rectangle A has 4 rows of 9 squares. Rectangle B has 9 rows of 4 squares. Which is true?
items.e: 4 × 9 = 36 and 9 × 4 = 36. Turning a rectangle does not change its area.

items.q: Which multiplication gives the number of squares in this rectangle?
items.e: There are 4 rows of 8 squares. 4 × 8 = 32 squares.

items.q: Only the top row and the left column of squares are drawn. How many squares would cover the whole rectangle?
items.e: The top row shows 8 squares in each row. The left column shows 6 rows. 6 × 8 = 48 squares.

items.q: A rectangle is covered by 7 rows of 1 m² squares, with 12 squares in each row. What is its area?
items.e: 7 rows of 12 squares: 7 × 12 = 84 squares, so the area is 84 m².

items.q: A rectangle is 36 m long and 15 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width: 36 × 15. Split 15 into 10 + 5: 36 × 10 = 360 and 36 × 5 = 180. 360 + 180 = 540 m². (Multiplying only tens × tens and ones × ones gives 330, which is too small.)

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the area of a bookmark?
items.e: A bookmark is small and area is the space inside, so use square centimetres. cm and m measure length; cm² and m² measure area.

items.q: What is the area of this rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width: 8 × 5 = 40 cm². (26 cm is the perimeter.)

items.q: What is the area of this rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width: 12 × 4 = 48 m². (32 m is the perimeter.)

items.q: What is the area of this rectangle?

items.q: What is the area of this rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width: 10 × 9 = 90 m². (38 m is the perimeter.)

items.q: A rectangle is 24 cm long and 6 cm wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width: 24 × 6. Split 24 into 20 + 4: 20 × 6 = 120 and 4 × 6 = 24. 120 + 24 = 144 cm².

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the area of a classroom floor?
items.e: A floor is big and area is the space inside, so use square metres. cm and m measure length; cm² and m² measure area.

items.q: A rectangle is 23 m long and 14 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width: 23 × 14. Split 14 into 10 + 4: 23 × 10 = 230 and 23 × 4 = 92. 230 + 92 = 322 m². (Multiplying only tens × tens and ones × ones gives 212, which is too small.)

items.q: Which rule gives the area of a rectangle?
items.e: Area counts the squares inside: rows × squares in each row, which is length × width. 2 × length + 2 × width is the perimeter.

items.q: Rectangle A is 12 cm by 6 cm. Rectangle B is 9 cm by 8 cm. Which has the bigger area?
items.e: A: 12 × 6 = 72 cm². B: 9 × 8 = 72 cm². The areas are the same, even though the shapes look different.

items.q: This is a square. What is its area?
items.e: The length and width of a square are the same: 15 × 15 = 225 cm². (60 cm is the perimeter.)

items.q: Rectangle A is 10 m by 7 m. Rectangle B is 9 m by 8 m. Which has the bigger area?
items.e: A: 10 × 7 = 70 m². B: 9 × 8 = 72 m². 72 − 70 = 2, so B is bigger by 2 m². (10 + 7 and 9 + 8 are both 17, but adding the sides does not give the area.)

items.q: A rectangle is 32 cm long and 25 cm wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width: 32 × 25. Split 25 into 20 + 5: 32 × 20 = 640 and 32 × 5 = 160. 640 + 160 = 800 cm². (Multiplying only tens × tens and ones × ones gives 610, which is too small.)

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the area of a soccer field?
items.e: A field is big and area is the space inside, so use square metres. cm and m measure length; cm² and m² measure area.

items.q: A rectangle is 35 m long and 8 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width: 35 × 8. Split 35 into 30 + 5: 30 × 8 = 240 and 5 × 8 = 40. 240 + 40 = 280 m².

items.q: A square has sides of 20 m. What is its area?
items.e: The length and width of a square are the same: 20 × 20 = 400 m². (80 m is the perimeter.)

items.q: What is the area of this rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width: 13 × 5 = 65 cm². (36 cm is the perimeter.)

items.q: What is the area of this rectangle?
items.e: Area = length × width: 11 × 6 = 66 cm². (34 cm is the perimeter.)

items.q: A rectangle is 15 cm long and 12 cm wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width: 15 × 12. Split 12 into 10 + 2: 15 × 10 = 150 and 15 × 2 = 30. 150 + 30 = 180 cm². (Multiplying only tens × tens and ones × ones gives 110, which is too small.)

items.q: What is the perimeter of this rectangle?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width: 30 + 16 = 46 cm. (15 × 8 = 120 cm² is the area.)

items.q: What is the perimeter of this rectangle?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width: 50 + 20 = 70 m. (25 × 10 = 250 m² is the area.)

items.q: A square has sides of 13 cm. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides: 4 × 13 = 52 cm. (13 × 13 = 169 cm² is the area.)

items.q: Each small square is 1 cm by 1 cm. What is the perimeter of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: Count the sides of the squares along the edge: 7 + 3 + 7 + 3 = 20 cm. (21 is the number of squares inside, the area. 16 counts the edge squares, and corner squares have two sides on the edge.)

items.q: Which unit is best for the length of the fence around a school playground?
items.e: A fence is a length around the edge, so use a length unit. A playground is big, so use metres. m² and cm² are for area.

items.q: What is the perimeter of this rectangle?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width: 24 + 10 = 34 m. (12 × 5 = 60 m² is the area.)

items.q: A rectangle is 2 m long and 60 cm wide. What is its perimeter in centimetres?
items.e: Change to one unit first: 2 m = 200 cm. Then 200 + 60 + 200 + 60 = 520 cm. (124 comes from adding 2 + 60 + 2 + 60 without changing metres to centimetres.)

items.q: A rectangle is 120 cm long and 75 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
items.e: Add all four sides: 120 + 75 + 120 + 75 = 390 cm. (Adding just 120 + 75 = 195 cm goes only halfway around.)

items.q: A rectangle is 250 m long and 130 m wide. What is its perimeter?
items.e: Add all four sides: 250 + 130 + 250 + 130 = 760 m. (Adding just 250 + 130 = 380 m goes only halfway around.)

items.q: A square has sides of 25 m. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides: 4 × 25 = 100 m. (25 × 25 = 625 m² is the area.)

items.q: What is the perimeter of this rectangle?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width: 18 + 8 = 26 cm. (9 × 4 = 36 cm² is the area.)

items.q: A square has a perimeter of 60 cm. How long is each side?
items.e: The 4 sides are equal: 60 ÷ 4 = 15 cm. Check: 4 × 15 = 60 cm.

items.q: Which rule gives the perimeter of a rectangle?
items.e: Perimeter is the distance around: two lengths and two widths. length × width is the area. length + width goes only halfway around.

items.q: What is the perimeter of this rectangle?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width: 22 + 14 = 36 cm. (11 × 7 = 77 cm² is the area.)

items.q: Each small square is 1 cm by 1 cm. What is the perimeter of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: Count the sides of the squares along the edge: 6 + 5 + 6 + 5 = 22 cm. (30 is the number of squares inside, the area. 18 counts the edge squares, and corner squares have two sides on the edge.)

items.q: A square has a perimeter of 36 m. How long is each side?
items.e: The 4 sides are equal: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 m. Check: 4 × 9 = 36 m.

items.q: A rectangle is 34 cm long and 16 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
items.e: Add all four sides: 34 + 16 + 34 + 16 = 100 cm. (Adding just 34 + 16 = 50 cm goes only halfway around.)

items.q: A rectangle is 3 m long and 80 cm wide. What is its perimeter in centimetres?
items.e: Change to one unit first: 3 m = 300 cm. Then 300 + 80 + 300 + 80 = 760 cm. (166 comes from adding 3 + 80 + 3 + 80 without changing metres to centimetres.)

items.q: A rectangle is 45 m long and 25 m wide. What is its perimeter?
items.e: Add all four sides: 45 + 25 + 45 + 25 = 140 m. (Adding just 45 + 25 = 70 m goes only halfway around.)

items.q: What is the perimeter of this rectangle?
items.e: Perimeter = 2 × length + 2 × width: 40 + 12 = 52 m. (20 × 6 = 120 m² is the area.)

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 91 m². One side is 7 m. How long is the other side?
items.e: Length × width = area, so think: 7 × ? = 91. 91 ÷ 7 = 13, so the side is 13 m. Check: 7 × 13 = 91 m².

items.q: What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: Length × width = area, so think: 6 × ? = 24. 24 ÷ 6 = 4, so the side is 4 cm. Check: 6 × 4 = 24 cm².

items.q: Liam covers a rectangle with 96 square tiles, with no gaps. There are 6 rows. How many tiles are in each row?
items.e: 6 rows × ? = 96. 96 ÷ 6 = 16 tiles in each row. Check: 6 × 16 = 96.

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 44 m. Its length is 14 m. What is its width?
items.e: The two lengths use 14 + 14 = 28 m. That leaves 44 − 28 = 16 m for the two widths. 16 ÷ 2 = 8 m. Check: 14 + 8 + 14 + 8 = 44 m.

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 cm. Its length is 9 cm. What is its width?
items.e: The two lengths use 9 + 9 = 18 cm. That leaves 30 − 18 = 12 cm for the two widths. 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm. Check: 9 + 6 + 9 + 6 = 30 cm.

items.q: What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: Length × width = area, so think: 8 × ? = 72. 72 ÷ 8 = 9, so the side is 9 m. Check: 8 × 9 = 72 m².

items.q: Chloe covers a rectangle with 84 square tiles, with no gaps. There are 7 rows. How many tiles are in each row?
items.e: 7 rows × ? = 84. 84 ÷ 7 = 12 tiles in each row. Check: 7 × 12 = 84.

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 144 m². One side is 9 m. How long is the other side?
items.e: Length × width = area, so think: 9 × ? = 144. 144 ÷ 9 = 16, so the side is 16 m. Check: 9 × 16 = 144 m².

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 36 m. Its length is 11 m. What is its width?
items.e: The two lengths use 11 + 11 = 22 m. That leaves 36 − 22 = 14 m for the two widths. 14 ÷ 2 = 7 m. Check: 11 + 7 + 11 + 7 = 36 m.

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 150 cm². One side is 10 cm. How long is the other side?
items.e: Length × width = area, so think: 10 × ? = 150. 150 ÷ 10 = 15, so the side is 15 cm. Check: 10 × 15 = 150 cm².

items.q: A square has an area of 64 cm². How long is each side?
items.e: Side × side = 64. 8 × 8 = 64, so each side is 8 cm. (64 ÷ 4 = 16 would be the side if 64 were the perimeter.)

items.q: A square has an area of 144 cm². How long is each side?
items.e: Side × side = 144. 12 × 12 = 144, so each side is 12 cm. (144 ÷ 4 = 36 would be the side if 144 were the perimeter.)

items.q: What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: Length × width = area, so think: 7 × ? = 63. 63 ÷ 7 = 9, so the side is 9 cm. Check: 7 × 9 = 63 cm².

items.q: What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: Length × width = area, so think: 9 × ? = 54. 54 ÷ 9 = 6, so the side is 6 m. Check: 9 × 6 = 54 m².

items.q: Wei covers a rectangle with 72 square tiles, with no gaps. There are 8 rows. How many tiles are in each row?
items.e: 8 rows × ? = 72. 72 ÷ 8 = 9 tiles in each row. Check: 8 × 9 = 72.

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 50 cm. Its length is 15 cm. What is its width?
items.e: The two lengths use 15 + 15 = 30 cm. That leaves 50 − 30 = 20 cm for the two widths. 20 ÷ 2 = 10 cm. Check: 15 + 10 + 15 + 10 = 50 cm.

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 96 cm². One side is 8 cm. How long is the other side?
items.e: Length × width = area, so think: 8 × ? = 96. 96 ÷ 8 = 12, so the side is 12 cm. Check: 8 × 12 = 96 cm².

items.q: What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: Length × width = area, so think: 8 × ? = 48. 48 ÷ 8 = 6, so the side is 6 cm. Check: 8 × 6 = 48 cm².

items.q: What is the length of the side marked ?
items.e: Length × width = area, so think: 7 × ? = 35. 35 ÷ 7 = 5, so the side is 5 m. Check: 7 × 5 = 35 m².

items.q: A square has an area of 100 m². How long is each side?
items.e: Side × side = 100. 10 × 10 = 100, so each side is 10 m. (100 ÷ 4 = 25 would be the side if 100 were the perimeter.)

sets.title: Same area, different perimeter and word problems

items.q: All these rectangles have an area of 36 m². Which has the shortest perimeter?
items.e: Perimeters: 6 by 6 = 24 m, 9 by 4 = 26 m, 12 by 3 = 30 m, 36 by 1 = 74 m. For the same area, the closer the shape is to a square, the shorter the perimeter.

items.q: Both rectangles have a perimeter of 24 m: one is 6 m by 6 m, the other is 10 m by 2 m. Which has the bigger area?
items.e: 6 × 6 = 36 m² and 10 × 2 = 20 m². The same perimeter can give very different areas.

items.q: Simran’s family stains a cedar deck at their cabin in Whistler. The deck is 8 m long and 6 m wide. One can of stain covers 12 m². How many cans do they need?
items.e: Area of the deck: 8 × 6 = 48 m². Each can covers 12 m²: 48 ÷ 12 = 4 cans.

items.q: Ava makes a poster for the Terry Fox Run. It is 60 cm long and 45 cm wide. What is its area?
A class banner for a BC Ferries field trip is 120 cm long and 80 cm wide. Ribbon goes all the way around the edge. How much ribbon is needed?
items.e: Ribbon goes around the edge: 120 + 80 + 120 + 80 = 400 cm. (200 cm goes only halfway around; 9600 cm² would be the area.)

items.q: A hay field in the Okanagan is 250 m long and 120 m wide. What is its area?
Owen’s bedroom is 4 m by 4 m. Arjun’s bedroom is 5 m by 3 m. Both have a perimeter of 16 m. Whose bedroom has the bigger area?
items.e: Owen: 4 × 4 = 16 m². Arjun: 5 × 3 = 15 m². 16 − 15 = 1, so Owen’s room is bigger by 1 m². The same perimeter does not mean the same area.

items.q: A soccer field in Surrey is 100 m long and 60 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: 100 × 60 = 6000 m². (320 m is the distance around the field; 600 is missing a zero.)

items.q: The reading corner is 6 m long and 5 m wide. Each carpet tile covers 1 m². The class has put down 18 tiles. How many more tiles are needed?
items.e: Whole corner: 6 × 5 = 30 tiles. Still needed: 30 − 18 = 12 tiles. (4 uses the perimeter, 22, instead of the area.)

items.q: Kai’s class has a plot at a community garden in Kamloops. It is 14 m long and 9 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width: 14 × 9 = 126 m². (46 m is the distance around, and 14 + 9 = 23 only adds two sides.)

items.q: Zara has 20 m of fence for a rectangular garden. Which garden gives the most area?
items.e: All use 20 m of fence. Areas: 5 × 5 = 25 m², 6 × 4 = 24 m², 7 × 3 = 21 m², 8 × 2 = 16 m². The square gives the most area.

items.q: A community garden plot in Kamloops is 14 m long and 9 m wide. How much fence goes all the way around it?
items.e: A fence goes around the edge: 14 + 9 + 14 + 9 = 46 m. (37 m leaves out one side; 126 m² is the area.)

items.q: How many different rectangles with whole-number sides have an area of 24 cm²? (A turned rectangle counts as the same one.)
items.e: 1 × 24, 2 × 12, 3 × 8 and 4 × 6: 4 rectangles. Their perimeters are all different: 50, 28, 22 and 20 cm. (8 counts each turned rectangle twice.)

items.q: Which rectangle has an area of 18 cm² and a perimeter of 18 cm?
items.e: 6 × 3 = 18 cm² and 6 + 3 + 6 + 3 = 18 cm. (9 by 2 has a perimeter of 22 cm; 5 by 4 and 7 by 2 have areas of 20 cm² and 14 cm².)

items.q: Leah’s bedroom floor is 5 m by 4 m. A rug 3 m by 2 m lies on it. What area of floor is not covered?
items.e: Floor: 5 × 4 = 20 m². Rug: 3 × 2 = 6 m². 20 − 6 = 14 m². (4 m² comes from (5 − 3) × (4 − 2), which takes away from the sides instead of the areas.)

items.q: Students in Nanaimo paint a mural on a school wall 9 m long and 3 m high. A window 2 m by 1 m is not painted. What area do they paint?
items.e: Wall: 9 × 3 = 27 m². Window: 2 × 1 = 2 m². 27 − 2 = 25 m². (29 adds the window instead of taking it away; 24 m is the perimeter of the wall.)

items.q: A rectangle is 6 cm by 4 cm. Both sides are doubled to 12 cm by 8 cm. What happens to the area?
items.e: Old area: 6 × 4 = 24 cm². New area: 12 × 8 = 96 cm². 96 ÷ 24 = 4, so it is 4 times as big. (The perimeter only doubles: 20 cm to 40 cm.)

items.q: A square photo frame has a perimeter of 64 cm. What is its area?
items.e: Each side: 64 ÷ 4 = 16 cm. Area: 16 × 16 = 256 cm². (4096 uses 64 as the side.)

items.q: Lucas’s rectangular vegetable bed has an area of 96 m². It is 12 m long. How wide is it?
items.e: 12 × ? = 96. 96 ÷ 12 = 8, so the bed is 8 m wide. (84 comes from subtracting: 96 − 12.)

items.q: Both rectangles have an area of 36 cm²: one is 9 cm by 4 cm, the other is 12 cm by 3 cm. Which has the longer perimeter?
items.e: 9 cm by 4 cm: 18 + 8 = 26 cm. 12 cm by 3 cm: 24 + 6 = 30 cm. The same area can have different perimeters.
